title: Adaptive delivery contracts and flow-control patterns for SIEM/webhook sinks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: External SIEM and webhook sinks (Splunk, Datadog, customer SIEMs) have wide variability in availability, rate limits, and ordering guarantees. Current forwarder implementation treats all sinks uniformly which leads to prolonged retry storms, tenant unfairness, and high egress/CPU cost during incidents. Goal: Define and implement an adaptive delivery contract model and flow-control primitives that allow the forwarder to negotiate QoS with sinks, apply tenant-aware rate limiting, degrade gracefully to archival, and provide strong observability and operational controls for Security/Platform teams.
acceptance_criteria: Forwarder supports configurable QoS tiers per sink: best-effort, guaranteed-retry (at-least-once within time window), and fire-and-forget
Per-tenant and per-sink adaptive rate limiter that respects origin quotas and sink-provided signals (429/Retry-After) with token-bucket + dynamic window adjustments
Built-in fallback to encrypted batched archival (S3) for sinks unavailable > X minutes, with replay API for customers and Platform
Delivery contract metadata propagated with events (sequence id, qos-tier, idempotency token) and visible in Console
End-to-end observability: success/failed/queued counts, per-tenant latency percentiles, retry-cause breakdown, and synthetic probe results on Datadog dashboard
Automated integration tests that simulate Splunk, Datadog, and flaky customer endpoints verifying ordering and retry semantics
Docs and runbook updated; oncall can change tenant throttles and trigger archival during incidents
design_decisions: Use explicit QoS tiers instead of attempting universal exactly-once; practical tradeoff for operational predictability
Sequence IDs per-tenant + per-stream to allow eventual ordering guarantees for guaranteed-retry tier; do not require global strict ordering
Soft-ack model where sinks can return 2xx for receipt, 202 for accepted-async, 4xx/5xx for retry/failure; platform treats 2xx and 202 as success for best-effort, only 2xx for guaranteed-retry
Expose tenant-level budget and a sink-level observed capacity metric so routing can prefer lower-cost/low-latency paths
Archival fallback signs batches with customer KMS key when required by compliance; stored with minimal metadata to reduce storage cost
tradeoffs: Not implementing strict exactly-once: avoids global coordination and large state, but clients needing absolute dedupe must deduplicate at consumer side using idempotency tokens
Adding sequence IDs increases event size and storage; we limit to a compact 64-bit monotonic per-stream counter to minimize overhead
Archival fallback increases storage costs and recovery complexity but prevents data loss and reduces retry storms against unstable sinks
Dynamic per-tenant throttling improves fairness but can introduce latency spikes for tenants who hit limits during cluster-wide load
implementation_notes: Introduce SinkContract object in forwarder config: qos_tier, retry_window_seconds, max_in_flight, archival_policy
Rate limiter: token-bucket with feedback loop adjusting refill rate using observed 429 frequency and average response latency
Add persisted per-stream sequence counter with compact commit log to avoid large DB writes on every event
Provide a control-plane API for Security/Platform to set temporary tenant or sink overrides
Instrumentation hooks: emit events to telemetry topic with delivery_state and reason codes for downstream aggregation
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Add SinkContract support and QoS metadata, route 5% of internal traffic to new forwarder variant; monitor synthetic probes
Phase 2: Enable adaptive rate limiter and archival fallback for non-production tenants; run chaos tests against simulated Splunk/Datadog endpoints
Phase 3: Gradually increase coverage to production tenants by percentage and enable per-tenant budgets UI in Console
Phase 4: Post-launch 2-week stabilization and iterate on Retry-window defaults based on observed failure modes
monitoring_and_metrics: SLOs to track: P99 end-to-end delivery latency for guaranteed-retry tier, fraction_of_events_archived, mean_time_to_resume_delivery
Datadog dashboard: synthetic probe latency + health, delivery contract violations over time
Alerting: sustained 429_rate > 1% for 5m triggers platform paging; high archive rate (>5% of events) triggers incident review
test_plan: Unit tests for rate limiter behavior under ideal and bursty sources
Integration tests: mocked Splunk/Datadog servers that return configurable 429/500 patterns and verify retry/backoff and archival
Load test: replay production traces with varied tenant distributions to validate fairness and CPU/egress cost impact
Chaos tests: network partitions to sinks and recovery simulations to validate replay correctness
Compliance test: verify archived batches are encrypted with expected KMS key and accessible via replay API
